title: Counteranion-mediated dynamic kinetic asymmetric fluorination to access sulfur-stereogenic center
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 24 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76036-y

The authors present a highly efficient strategy to synthesize sulfonimidoyl fluorides through dynamic kinetic asymmetric fluorination at mild reaction conditions. This one-pot process, involving sequential direct fluorination, hydrolysis, and asymmetric fluorination, delivers a wide range of enantioenriched S(VI) compounds with high enantioselectivities.

title: Microwave-field quantum metrology with inherent robustness against detection losses enabled by Rydberg interactions
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 24 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76016-2

Rydberg atoms provide both quantum metrological and computational applications, but despite the efforts, the combination of the two has not yet translated into practical applications. Here, the authors demonstrate a microwave-sensing protocol based on collective Rydberg states, where the interatomic interactions allow implementation of inherent error protection.

title: A benchmark study of vision and pathology foundation models for computational pathology
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 24 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76004-6

The comparative performance and generalisability of pathology foundation models remain largely unexamined. Here, the authors benchmark 32 AI pathology foundation models across large cancer datasets, showing that generalisation in computational pathology is heterogeneous and task-dependent regardless of dataset scale, but ensemble-based approaches can combine the strengths of different models.

title: A natural solution from caterpillar cuticles for flexible impact-resistant materials
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 24 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75849-1

Here, authors explore the energy dissipation mechanism in the cuticle of Ostrinia furnacalis (Asian corn borer) to identify key structural proteins, FCSP-1 and FCSP-2, which undergo liquid-liquid phase separation to form flexible, impact-resistant materials.

title: CDC7 and APC/C<sup>Cdh1</sup> gate distinct routes to initiate DNA replication
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 24 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75804-0

Human DNA replication initiation is triggered at a tunable CDK2/1 activity threshold gated by two parallel pathways. DBF4-CDC7 activity enables origin firing independent of APC/CCdh1 inactivation by phosphorylating MCMs.

title: Upwind terrestrial influences on soil moisture variability across South America
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 24 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75637-x

The study applies deep learning and moisture tracking and finds that Amazonian vegetation shapes soil moisture thousands of kilometers downwind across South America, sustaining distant farmland and showing how forest loss could worsen drought risk.

title: Field-to-forest fungal spillover is a biotic edge effect of coffee in Costa Rica
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 24 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75178-3

Agriculture can affect wild ecosystems when crop microbes spread to nearby plants. Here, coffee-associated fungi were found to disproportionately colonize wild relatives of coffee near forest–farm borders.

title: RETROFIT: Reference-free deconvolution of cell-type mixtures in spatial transcriptomics
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 24 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-74928-7

Spatial transcriptomics enables mapping of gene expression in tissues, but deconvolving mixed cell populations remains challenging. Here, the authors introduce RETROFIT, a reference-free Bayesian method that infers cell-type composition and expression without relying on external references.
